touches.text: The librarian owns every tree and delegates ownership of some to the devices that learn: CodeMother, chart, any learning block holds its own trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). Why: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both. (Akien 2026-11-05)

Cross-domain questions: a special kind of question, inherently cross domain (or cognition questions), not domain specific. "How might that work?" is Akien's number one. They are not design questions: a design question is a spec choice waiting on Akien (cairn question, CairnCommons/questions/). (Akien 2026-11-05)

A question is a node in the one list (4.3.1.8.1). Questions can belong to devices, and two devices can have the same question: both hold the same node. A device that owns a question is a delegate, because all knowledge belongs ultimately to the librarian (4.3.1.6). Owning a question = holding a tree for it, with that device's own weights.

The answers to cross-domain questions are what get embedded (4.3.1.8.1.1): an answer from any domain lands in that question's tree as a pattern, so a later search under the same question finds patterns from other domains ("which often initiates a cross domain search", Akien 2026-07-14).

The corpus is a git JSON file beside the librarian's code (shareable spec, 4.3.4); the question trees are derived from it. Every entry carries its origin: verbatim (Akien's words, with date and source) or proposed (by CC, by Gemini, ...). All questions are included; the origin keeps his words apart. (Akien 2026-11-05: "we can include all the questions. i expect i have a couple of hundred in my own head.")

NOT HOW IT IS NOW (measured 2026-11-05): the corpus lives in CodeMother (cairn/devices/codemother/cognition_questions.json, embedded by seed_trees.py) with 13 of UU's 18 verbatim questions (Q-cog-014..018 lost in the move), Akien's 3 from Novelty.txt, and 11 Gemini-worded questions labelled "Akien verbatim".
Watcher face: watches the code and the builders' work over time, reasons over it with graph trees (deposited with the librarian), and learns the failure modes.
Learns from: code, chat logs, books, past projects, CC's failure modes.
